create.name: Rev. angel Kyodo williams
create.bio:
Rev. angel Kyodo williams is a Zen priest, author and teacher whose work brings meditation practice and the pursuit of justice together. A Black woman of mixed heritage, she founded the Center for Transformative Change and has spent many years training and coaching people in communities, workplaces and institutions to bring what they think, feel and do into line with one another. Her guiding phrase is that love and justice are not two: in her view inner change and collective change depend on each other.

Her first book, Being Black, a Zen guide to meeting life with courage and grace, reached its twentieth anniversary in 2020. She later wrote Radical Dharma: Talking Race, Love and Liberation with two fellow practitioners of colour, a book on how race and privilege show up in Buddhist, yoga and other spiritual communities, and it grew into a series of circles and conversations. Today she hosts a monthly online half-day sit, with long stretches of silent practice and a public talk, and runs 27 Days of Change, a guided programme linking personal practice with social change. She has also designed a mindfulness training programme and for several years led a week-long retreat on Molokai in Hawaii. Her YouTube channel gathers talks on Zen, contemplation and change.
